candidates.topic: Amazon acetaminophen recall (Aurobindo Pharma) — part of expanding FDA recall pattern
candidates.recommended_angle: Frame as latest entry in expanding FDA recall pattern; use consumer-facing trending hook to re-explain how to check if your bottle is affected and why recalls clustered fall 2026.
candidates.why_now: Real-time Google Trends breakout with confirmed news driver (USA Today); 4+ other FDA recalls landed since original recall-pattern piece ran 10/09.
candidates.primary_headline: Amazon-Sold Acetaminophen Recalled — Here's What to Know About the Growing 2026 FDA Recall Wave
candidates.next_steps: Verify primary FDA.gov recall notice and lot numbers/NDC codes before publishing; corroborate USA Today report.
integrity_flags: Primary FDA.gov recall notice not directly retrieved this session — confirmed via USA Today and MedShadow Foundation only; verify lot numbers/NDC codes against FDA.gov before publishing.
candidates.trend_score_reason: Real-time Google Trends breakout + USA Today confirmation + 5th major FDA consumer recall since Oct 7.
candidates.opportunity_score_reason: Consumer-facing safety explainer with direct Q&A fit ('is my product affected'); strong information-seeking intent.
candidates.discover_score_reason: Specific named entity, product-centric query, direct consumer safety question = strong AI-citation candidate once primary FDA source linked.
candidates.notes: Hold publish until FDA.gov notice directly retrieved; estimated 700-900 words; news explainer format with checklist graphic.

fact_check.checked_against: Google Trends 'amazon acetaminophen recall aurobindo pharma' breakout with USA Today Why-line; MedShadow Foundation FDA recall roundup listing Amazon Acetaminophen alongside eye drops and glutathione; multiple additional FDA recall headlines in News Radar (Gatorade, smoked fish, baby sleep aid, supplement powder, pre-workout) supporting 'recall wave' framing

candidates.topic: West Nile virus — North Carolina deaths
candidates.allowed_category: Infectious disease / public health and epidemiology
candidates.recommended_angle: Use breaking local fatality report as hook for national-scope explainer — most existing coverage is local/regional; opportunity for broader symptoms/prevention/risk-factor piece citing CDC surveillance data.
candidates.why_now: Real-time Google Trends breakout with confirmed WRAL reporting of two deaths; distinct from ongoing measles-outbreak story already covered twice this week — different pathogen, different public-health angle.
candidates.primary_headline: West Nile Virus Has Killed Two People in North Carolina — What to Know as Cases Rise
candidates.next_steps: Corroborate death count with NC DHHS or CDC ArboNET surveillance data before publishing exact case/death numbers.
integrity_flags: WRAL is currently sole named source for death count — corroborate against NC DHHS or CDC ArboNET surveillance data before publishing exact case/death numbers.
candidates.trend_score_reason: Real-time Google Trends breakout + confirmed WRAL fatality report + CDC national case tracking available.
candidates.opportunity_score_reason: Informational + evaluative intent; maps to direct queries ('West Nile virus symptoms', 'is it dangerous'); strong public-health explainer fit.
candidates.discover_score_reason: Specific seasonal disease, strong AI-citation fit; CDC primary source readily available; direct symptom/prevention queries.
candidates.notes: Estimated 700-900 words; news explainer format; US map of WNV activity + mosquito prevention infographic recommended.

issues: The claim that an 'ongoing measles-outbreak story already covered twice this week' exists is not supported by anything in the evidence provided — this comparison is unverifiable from the signal data.
fact_check.checked_against: Google Trends 'west nile virus north carolina' breakout with WRAL Why-line confirming two deaths; no corroborating CDC or NC DHHS figures present in evidence, consistent with EXISTING FLAGS

candidates.topic: Clinical trial diversity & the women's health data gap
candidates.recommended_angle: Evaluative — two independent industry analyses (Clinical Trials Arena, Penn LDI) point to same persistent gap; use as news hook for explainer on why trial diversity matters for drug safety/efficacy and what's changing.
candidates.why_now: Two independent analyses published on converging theme; FDA/NIH diversity action plans provide policy context; addresses systemic gap in evidence base.
candidates.primary_headline: Why Clinical Trials Still Underrepresent Women — and What's Being Done About It
candidates.next_steps: Identify and contact named clinical researcher or health policy researcher from Penn LDI piece for expert commentary; verify statistics trace to original FDA/NIH source documents.
integrity_flags: Ensure any statistics cited trace back to original FDA/NIH diversity action plans rather than secondary paraphrase.
candidates.trend_score_reason: Two independent analyses converging on same theme; moderate search volume for 'clinical trial diversity women' queries.
candidates.opportunity_score_reason: Evaluative/explainer opportunity; addresses evidence gap; policy context adds relevance; good internal linking to drug-safety pieces.
candidates.discover_score_reason: Moderate discover potential — niche policy topic with healthcare relevance; evergreen framing supports sustained AI citation.
candidates.notes: Estimated 500-650 words; evergreen explainer format. Medium SERP difficulty. Requires named researcher context per health-sourcing rules.

issues: Framing credits 'FDA/NIH diversity action plans' for policy context, but the only action-plan document in evidence (Milken Institute's 'Enabling Access to Clinical Research') is not an FDA or NIH document — this attribution overstates the sourcing.
fact_check.checked_against: Clinical Trials Arena and Penn LDI articles both dated 10/12/2026 in News Radar converging on trial diversity/women's health gap; Milken Institute policy report present but not confirmed as FDA/NIH-authored
